blocks.text: An inductor (also called a coil or choke) is a two-terminal component with a large self-inductance and negligible resistance; it stores energy in a magnetic field while current flows through it. It is used to slow down current surges or spikes by temporarily storing energy and releasing it back into the circuit.

Suppose an inductor L is connected to an AC source of frequency f (Fig 17.7 a) and the current is I = Io sin(wt) (17.13). The changing current sets up a back emf in the coil of magnitude L dI/dt, and the applied voltage must equal it: V = L (d/dt)(Io sin(wt)) = L Io w cos(wt) (17.14). With Vo = w L Io, V = Vo cos(wt) = Vo sin(wt + pi/2) (17.15). So the voltage across an inductor leads the current by 90 degrees (pi/2 rad); in other words, the current in an inductor lags the voltage by 90 degrees (Figs 17.7 b and c).

blocks.title: Inductive reactance
blocks.text: The opposition offered by an inductor is its inductive reactance, XL = Vrms / Irms (17.16). Since Vrms = 0.707 Vo, Irms = 0.707 Io and Vo = w L Io, XL = w L = 2 pi f L (17.17). Its unit is the ohm.
XL is directly proportional to both the frequency and the inductance. For DC, f = 0, so XL = 0; at high frequency XL is large. An inductor therefore passes DC but opposes (blocks) high-frequency AC.

The average power dissipated in a pure inductor is zero. The inductor does not consume power: it stores energy in its magnetic field during part of each cycle and returns it to the source when the field collapses. Because V and I differ in phase by 90 degrees, the average power per cycle is zero. An inductor can therefore control AC without consuming energy.

blocks.title: Phase of the power
blocks.text: The book says the instantaneous power in an inductive circuit is zero. In fact the instantaneous power VI swings positive and negative (energy flows in and out of the magnetic field); it is the average over a cycle that is zero.

A 400 mH coil of negligible resistance carries an rms current of 6 mA at 1 kHz. Find the rms voltage across it. Solution: XL = 2 pi f L = 2 x 3.14 x 1000 Hz x 0.400 H = 2512 ohm, so Vrms = Irms XL = (6 x 10^-3 A)(2512 ohm) = 15 V.

blocks.title: For your information
blocks.text: dI/dt is the rate of change of current with time, the slope of the I-t graph. Chokes come in several types: filter chokes, high-frequency chokes, radio-frequency chokes and AC-controlling chokes (shown in the book as photographs).

blocks.prompt: What happens to the reactance of an inductor if the frequency is doubled?
blocks.explanation: It doubles, because XL = 2 pi f L is proportional to f.

items: Inductor: V leads I by 90 degrees (I lags V).
XL = wL = 2 pi f L: zero for DC, large at high f.
Average power in a pure inductor = 0.
